RIMANDO, CESO Ill Regional Director Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) MIMAROPA REGION No. 822, Quezon Avenue, Brgy. Paligsahan, Quezon City Dear RD Rimando: This refers to your memorandum dated November 18, 2024, regarding the concems of stakeholders of the Pamilihang Bayan ng San Jose, Occidental Mindoro, enumerated as follows: I. 2. 3. 4. What are the requisites for the implementation of a local project such as the construction of a public market, funded by the National Government and implemented by the DPWH; Can the construction project continue despite lack of proper prior consultation to the stakeholders; Do we really need to secure authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan prior to the construction and implementation of the project; What are the delineation of functions between the Executive and Legislative. Below are this level's responses to the queries: First, the implementation of government projects, including those funded by the National Govemment and implemented by DPWH, must comply with the Local Govemment Code (LGC) of 1991. Specifically, Section 271 mandates prior consultation before execution, particularly for projects with significant environmental and social impact. Section 262 further emphasizes the duty of agencies to consider potential adverse effects on resources and communities. Section 27. Prior Consultations Required. - No project or program shall be implemented by govemment authorities unless the consultations mentioned in Sections 2 (c) and 26 hereof are complied with, and prior approval of the sanggunian concerned is obtained: Provided, That occupants in areas where such projects are to be implemented shall not be evicted unless appropriate relocation sites have been provided, in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. 2 Section 26. Duty Of National Government Agencies in the Maintenance of Ecological Balance. - It shall be the duty of every national agency or government-owned or controlled corporation authorizing or involved in the planning and implementation of any project or program that may cause pollution, climatic change, depletion of non-renewable resources, loss Of crop land, rangeland, or forest cover, and extinction of animal or plant species, to consult with the local government units, nongovernmental organizations, and other sectors concerned and explain the goals and objectives of the project or program, its impact upon the people and the community in terms of environmental or ecological balance, and tie measures that will be undertaken to prevent or minimize the adverse effects thereof. "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Tel. (02) 8876-3454

Second, construction without prior consultation, mandatory consultations with stakeholders, including LGUs, non-governmental organizations. and affected communities, are required for projects that may cause environmental or social disturbances. Failure to comply may render the project illegal and hold officials accountable. In Lina vs. Pan03, the Supreme Coud held that Section 27 of the Local Government Code of 1991 should be read in conjunction with Section 26 thereof. Thus, the projects and programs mentioned in Section 27 should be interpreted to mean projects and programs whose effects are among those enumerated in Section 26 and 27, to wit, those that: (I) may cause pollution; (2) may bring about climate change; (3) may cause the depletion of non-renewable resources; (4) may result in loss of crop land, rangeland, or forest cover; (5) may eradicate certain animal or plant species and (6) other projects or programs that may call for the eviction of a particular group of people residing in the locality where these will be implemented. In light of the foregoing, considering that the construction of a public market may cause pollution as it is common knowledge that public markets produce waste, we opine that such project needs prior consultation with the stakeholders. Third, Sec. 27 of the LGC expressly mentions that prior approval of the sanggunian concemed should be obtained. Finally, to address the fourth query on the delineation of functions between executive and legislative, we provide you with this guidance: The Municipal Mayor, as chief executive, supervises municipal operations, enforces laws, manages resources, and ensures the delivery of services per Sections 17 and 444 of the LGC. The Vice-Mayor presides over the Sangguniang Bayan, assumes the mayor's offce if necessary, and exercises powers granted by law (Section 445, LGC). The Sangguniang Bayan, as the legislative body, enacts ordinances, approves resolutions, and oversees municipal development in line with Section 447 of the LGC. It holds regulatory and environmental protection functions. This opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent agencies and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, ATTY. ROMEO P. ENITEZ Undersecretary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs CC: DILG Occidental Mirujoro 3 G.R.
